capabilities: Collect RSS and Atom feeds into a local SQLite database with OPML and list import
Screen papers in To screen, Following, Saved, Skipped, and Expired baskets
Rank pending papers with a local TF-IDF and logistic-regression model trained on reading decisions
Translate paper titles via Google web translation or an OpenAI-compatible LLM
Analyze reading states and compare interest rates across feeds
disambiguation: Not a reference manager or full-text database; it only handles the screening step between new papers arriving and deciding what deserves a closer read.
extras: Desktop-only; requires Obsidian 1.13.0+ with a bundled Node.js 22.16+ runtime exposing node:sqlite, and there is no sql.js fallback. Google translation uses an unofficial web API and may be rate-limited or inaccurate. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
problem: Researchers following many journal and lab feeds get more new papers than they can inspect, and Obsidian has no built-in way to collect, screen, and prioritize them in one local queue.

relations.evidence: Choose Google web translation (default) or an OpenAI-compatible LLM under Title translation.
Optionally review only pending papers with a user-configured OpenAI-compatible LLM.

summary: Desktop RSS/Atom reader that collects academic feeds into a local SQLite database, triages papers in five baskets, and ranks them from your reading decisions.
